chunks: And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Mundhir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: "My wife gave me money for me to use as I wished. May I buy a bondwoman with her money and have relations with her?"
He عليه السلام said: "No. She only gave it to you so that her eye might be comforted, while you intend to make her eye burn with grief."

key_terms.أَطَؤُهَا: to have sexual relations with her
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a bondwoman or female slave being considered for purchase
key_terms.امْرَأَتِي: my wife; the spouse whose property and emotional interest are central in the ruling
key_terms.تُسْخِنَ عَيْنَهَا: to make her eye burn; meaning to cause her distress and sorrow
key_terms.لِتَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا: so that her eye may be comforted; meaning to bring her happiness and reassurance
key_terms.مَالًا: money or property entrusted for use

ai.seo_question: Can a husband use his wife's money to buy a bondwoman for himself?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling rooted in consideration of the wife's intent and emotional right within marriage. The Imam عليه السلام forbids using the wife's money in a way that would harm her and undermine the comfort and goodwill for which she entrusted it.
